title: Christina Ricci Exposes 30‑Year Grudge With ‘Mermaids’ Co‑Star Cher, Says She Still Holds a Grudge
body:
Christina Ricci let slip on Tuesday night that a feud with pop legend Cher, which began on the set of the 1990 fantasy film Mermaids, still simmers after three decades, and the singer appears unwilling to let the past go. Speaking on Watch What Happens Live with Andy Cohen, Ricci described how a once‑close friendship deteriorated into a lingering grudge that has shaped both women’s recollections of the movie and its aftermath.

The tension traces back to the early‑1990s when Ricci, then a teenage breakout star of The Addams Family, was cast as the youngest of three sisters in Mermaids, starring Cher as a single mother navigating love and loss. According to Ricci, the two initially bonded over music and fashion, sharing backstage moments and swapping stories about the pressures of fame. “We were having a lot of fun,” Ricci recalled, “and I thought we were going to be friends for life.” However, a series of misunderstandings—some reportedly stemming from differing work styles and a clash of personalities—escalated into a full‑blown argument that left both parties feeling betrayed.

Ricci said the rift deepened when Cher, who was already an established icon, allegedly “went cold” after the film’s release, refusing to acknowledge Ricci in public appearances or interviews. “She holds a grudge,” Ricci said bluntly, adding that she has never received an invitation to any of Cher’s events, nor a simple greeting when they cross paths at industry gatherings. The actress noted that while time has softened many Hollywood feuds, this particular dispute feels “frozen in place,” with Cher seemingly unwilling to make amends.

Industry insiders suggest that the fallout may have been amplified by the intense media scrutiny surrounding Mermaids, a film that received mixed reviews but became a cultural touchstone for its soundtrack and fashion. The movie’s promotional tour forced both women into a relentless schedule of talk‑show rounds and press junkets, a setting ripe for miscommunication. Moreover, the generational gap—Cher’s established career versus Ricci’s emerging stardom—could have contributed to differing expectations about respect, collaboration, and public representation. Some former crew members have hinted that on‑set tensions were palpable, describing a “charged atmosphere” that persisted beyond filming.

The lingering animosity has broader implications for how Hollywood navigates personal conflicts in the public eye. In an era where social media can quickly transform private disagreements into viral narratives, the Ricci‑Cher saga underscores the difficulty of reconciling past grievances when both parties have cultivated distinct brand identities. While Ricci appears comfortable airing the story, perhaps as a means of closure, Cher’s silence suggests a strategic choice to avoid reigniting the drama. Critics note that the reluctance to address the issue publicly may be rooted in a desire to protect her legacy, especially as she continues to command massive touring revenues and a renewed presence in television.

Looking ahead, the possibility of reconciliation remains uncertain. Ricci hinted that she would welcome an olive branch, stating, “If she ever wants to talk, I’m open.” Yet she also acknowledged that the industry’s fast‑paced nature often leaves little room for personal healing. As both women continue to evolve—Ricci taking on more mature, dramatic roles and Cher maintaining a dominant presence in music and television—their shared history may linger as a footnote rather than a headline. Still, the revelation serves as a reminder that even iconic collaborations can fracture, and that the passage of time does not always mend broken ties.
